subject.title: feat(gateway): pre-handshake WS verifyClient with Sec-Fetch-Site and forwarded-header hardening

question: Should Gateway permanently enforce forwarded-header contradiction and protocol-mismatch checks before the WebSocket handshake, and should those checks remain compatibility-preserving opt-ins under gateway.security or become intentional default-on policy?
rationale: This changes a network trust boundary and adds three durable configuration contracts; code review cannot choose the intended rejection defaults, namespace, and relationship to existing post-handshake Origin policy without owner intent.

options.title: Preserve compatibility with approved opt-ins
options.body: Keep pre-handshake validation, gate every newly rejecting check behind clearly documented settings, and approve one canonical gateway.security contract before merge.

options.title: Adopt default-on hardening
options.body: Make selected checks unconditional only with explicit owner acceptance, upgrade documentation, and proof covering existing trusted-proxy arrangements.

options.title: Pause for unified Origin policy
options.body: Hold this PR until the admission and configuration design can be consolidated with the related allowed-origin work in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/98924.

recommendation.title: Preserve compatibility with approved opt-ins
recommendation.body: Keep pre-handshake validation, gate every newly rejecting check behind clearly documented settings, and approve one canonical gateway.security contract before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent history and the discussion route the Gateway browser-Origin and admission-policy boundary to steipete.
